bull.t: Strong revenue growth and cloud adoption
bull.b: Sustained growth in total and cloud revenue indicates expanding adoption of JFrog’s platform and a durable shift toward recurring SaaS delivery. Raised full-year guidance and increasing cloud mix support continued scalability and customer migration.

bull.t: Enterprise expansion, retention and security attach
bull.b: Large-account growth, strong net dollar retention and security upsell activity demonstrate meaningful platform expansion within existing customers. These trends can support recurring revenue durability, higher wallet share and stronger competitive positioning.

bull.t: Robust cash generation and low leverage
bull.b: Strong operating and free cash flow provides resources for product investment, security improvements and strategic growth without relying heavily on external financing. Very low leverage also preserves flexibility through changing software spending conditions.

bear.b: Although losses have narrowed, JFrog has not yet demonstrated sustained GAAP profitability. Continued losses can limit reported returns and make long-term earnings conversion dependent on maintaining growth, margin discipline and effective expense control.

The incident highlights ongoing security, remediation and reputational risks in customer-managed deployments. Significant self-hosted exposure increases operational complexity and may require sustained investment to protect trust and accelerate safer cloud or hybrid migration.

bear.t: Revenue visibility affected by usage and deal timing
bear.b: Variable consumption, delayed commitments and shifting large-deal timing can make revenue conversion less predictable even with strong demand and RPO growth. Lower visibility may complicate planning and produce uneven execution across reporting periods.
